cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The first subpopulation fixture defined the subpopulation as x2 > 5 on the main design. It cut across strata and PSUs as intended, but left every PSU non-empty, so the design structure was unchanged and the correct approach (subsetting the design) and the incorrect one (filtering the rows first) produced byte-identical standard errors.
impact: Any test asserting that the two approaches differ would have been vacuous while appearing to guard the exact defect the release exists to remove. The difference only appears when the subpopulation empties whole PSUs, which needs three PSUs per stratum, since the main fixture has two per stratum for BRR and dropping one would collapse into a lonely-PSU error instead.
lesson: A fixture built to show that two approaches differ must be checked to actually make them differ, and that check belongs in the generator rather than in the test. The generator now asserts the subpopulation paths disagree and that provided replicate weights reproduce BRR exactly, so a fixture that stops discriminating fails at generation instead of turning a downstream assertion silently green.

cause: A capability audit against the stated product priorities showed the plan was inverted. The top P0 item -- a unified result contract covering coefficients, intervals, marginal effects, diagnostics and figure projection -- is not implemented, while survey design, a single P2 line item, carried roughly seventy percent of the version's blocks. Measured evidence: backend/workbench/contracts/model/ holds one contract per family rather than one shared contract, and the closed three-value result_shape enum is why.
impact: Continuing as planned would have deferred the highest-priority foundation by a full version while adding survey support family by family. About half of block 2 is foundation work independent of survey (opening result_shape, the orthogonal Design x Estimator x Variance engine, the R oracle harness), so the natural cut is at the end of block 2.
lesson: Re-audit scope against stated priorities before each large block, not only at version kickoff. A plan can be internally coherent and still be inverted relative to what matters, and block-by-block momentum hides that. The audit also had to distinguish infrastructure wearing a feature's name from the feature itself, which is what made a clean cut point visible.

cause: Six numerical conventions in R's survey package were guessed wrong and only external comparison caught them: intervals use the residual design df (degf-p+1=6, t=2.447) not degf; the adjusted Wald carries no ddf/degf rescaling; BRR uses the smallest Hadamard order that is a multiple of four above the stratum count (12, not the 16 a power-of-two rule gives); replicate deviations centre on the replicate mean because survey.replicates.mse defaults to FALSE; the population variance is a weighted mean of squared deviations corrected by n/(n-1) on the observation count, not divided by summed weights; and the design-effect reference variance carries a finite-population correction in which summed weights stand in for population size.
impact: Each wrong choice produced a plausible number: the variance definition was out by 1.2%, close enough to read as rounding, and the design effect by 9%. An internal-consistency suite would have passed on all six.
lesson: These are choices the reference implementation made, not results the statistics dictate. A capability claiming to match established software has to compare against it, because a self-consistent implementation of the wrong convention is indistinguishable from a correct one.

cause: BRR's standard error depends on which balanced set of half-samples is used. On the committed fixture R returns 1.62518598 from its 12-replicate matrix, 1.70845732 from a 20-replicate one, and a 16-replicate Sylvester matrix gives a third. All are valid.
impact: Matching R bit for bit was not a well-formed claim for BRR until the balanced set was pinned. Chasing the gap as a defect would have ended in a wrong fix or a loosened tolerance.
lesson: Establish that a reference value is unique before treating a mismatch as a defect. Where a method admits several valid answers the oracle must fix the choice and the result must record it; a BRR standard error reported without naming its balanced set is under-specified.

cause: test_engine_capabilities.py and test_ols_weights_v186.py import workbench.engine.stages.estimation first, initialising engine.stages, which imports statistical_tests, which imports orchestrator, which imports engine.stages.statistical_tests while it is still initialising. Confirmed pre-existing by stashing the working changes and reproducing on the baseline.
impact: These files run only inside the full suite, where another module imports orchestrator first. Re-running a single failing test fails with an ImportError resembling fresh breakage, and cost time in this line before being identified as pre-existing.
lesson: A suite that passes in only one collection order hides which change caused a failure. Worth breaking the cycle in its own scope rather than inside a feature block.

cause: Blocks 2 and 3 deliver the design-variance engine, open the result_shape extension point, and wire four families to it.
impact: A real run declaring strata, PSU and a sampling weight reports standard errors matching R's svyglm to 1e-8, where the naive fit reported 0.0850 against a true 0.1773 with identical coefficients. Backend 4662 passed / 2 skipped / 1 xfailed against 4638 after block 1; golden 18 passed, no golden file modified.
lesson: Wiring the first families in the same block as the engine surfaced a second copy of the refusal in econometrics/runner.py that unit tests could not reach, because they mock that layer. An engine verified only through its own tests would have shipped looking complete while remaining unreachable.
